verdict.rationale: Flagsmith Experimentation collects events from your application into a managed data warehouse and analyzes results with a built-in Bayesian engine, which suggests experiments can draw on your own ingested events. The evidence never describes how metrics are defined, and the warehouse is Flagsmith-managed rather than the customer's own tables. The 'your own analytics platform' route is an external workaround and earns no credit. missing for 10: documented metric-definition workflow, connection to customer-owned warehouse tables, transparency into metric computation (vs. a managed store), independent corroboration

support.subject: As a product manager, I can define experiment metrics from my own data — warehouse tables or ingested events — instead of a black-box metric store

citations.quote: collect events from your application into a managed data warehouse, and read the results with a built-in Bayesian statistics engine.
